text.p: Europe's biggest mobile phone maker Nokia Oy said Thursday that its 1996 profits fell in line with market expectations but raised its dividend and predicted strong growth and profitability in 1997.

Nokia said profit before tax and minority interests fell 21 percent to 3.90 billion Finnish markka ($786 million) from 4.93 billion ($1.3 billion) in 1995, recovering in the second half after logistical problems in its fast-growing mobile business hit first-half earnings.
Operating profits surged more than 70 percent over the year to 1.74 billion markka ($351 million) in the fourth quarter.
Nokia raised its dividend to 3.50 markka (71 cents) from 3.00 markka (60 cents) last year.

Nokia's total net sales rose to 39.32 billion markka ($7.9 billion) from 36.81 billion ($7.4 billion). Sales in telecommunications infrastructure rose 29 percent, while mobile phones sales grew by 34 percent.
